chitchat: "Doorways. That's all. I don't ask what's behind them, that's a different department."
"It's a job. You don't have to like the ledger to eat off it."
description: A damp, apologetic man with a clipboard held against his chest like a shield, counting doorways on Foundry Way and writing each one down. He has a lanyard that has never once been checked and the specific patience of somebody paid by the hour to do something pointless.

bye.text: He goes back to the doorways.

root.first: He looks up from the clipboard, sees somebody who isn't a doorway, and is briefly at a loss. "Ah. Are you — is this your door?"
root.text: He has moved eleven feet along the street and is counting again. "Still going. Long street."

why.text:
"Doorways." He shows you the clipboard as though it settles something. "Every one on the Row, and whether it opens. I don't ask what's behind them. That's a different department and I have never met anybody from it."

He writes another number down.

"It's a job. You don't have to like the ledger to eat off it."

clothing_layers: a municipal weatherproof two sizes too big
a knitted tie under a damp collar
shoes that were never meant to be walked in this much

name: Wexley Tolliver
